However, muscle damage is substantially attenuated over time via the repeated bout effect (148); thus, the implications in this regard are questionable for well-trained lifters, although it is possible that relatively modest myofiber disruptions from eccentric training may confer a hypertrophic effect. It also is conceivable that early-phase myodamage may induce greater satellite cell responses that ultimately drive greater long-term growth. The relevance of muscle damage in eccentric training-related hypertrophic adaptations remains speculative.
